audits.title: Using multifaceted education to improve management in acute viral bronchiolitis.
audits.standard: SIGN bronchiolitis guidelines and local hospital guidelines
audits.setting: Twelve acute paediatric departments across Wales

cycle1.result: Compliance: investigations 50% (46% to 53%), management 65% (61% to 68%), overall 38% (37% to 39%).

audits.intervention: Nationwide multifaceted education bundle after dissemination of first audit results.

cycle2.result: Compliance: investigations 71% (68% to 74%), management 74% (71% to 77%), overall 59% (56% to 62%).

audits.other_findings: 1599 infants in total; severity was equivalent in both years.
audits.citation: Murch H, Oakley J, Pierrepoint M, Powell C. Using multifaceted education to improve management in acute viral bronchiolitis. Arch Dis Child. 2015;100(7):654-658. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2014-307353. PMID: 25888695.

audits.title: Reducing unnecessary chest X-rays, antibiotics and bronchodilators through implementation of the NICE bronchiolitis guideline.
audits.setting: Secondary paediatric unit, University Hospital North Tees, Stockton-on-Tees

cycle1.result: Chest X-ray 20%, antibiotics 22%, inhaled/nebulised treatment 30%; overall NICE compliance 28%.

audits.intervention: Educational sessions for clinicians and nurses on appropriate and inappropriate bronchiolitis management with NICE guideline implementation.

cycle2.result: Chest X-ray 4%, antibiotics 6%, inhaled/nebulised treatment 16%; overall NICE compliance 63%.

audits.citation: Breakell R, Thorndyke B, Clennett J, Harkensee C. Reducing unnecessary chest X-rays, antibiotics and bronchodilators through implementation of the NICE bronchiolitis guideline. Eur J Pediatr. 2018;177(1):47-51. doi:10.1007/s00431-017-3034-5. PMID: 29080051.

audits.title: Quality improvement project to decrease unnecessary investigations in infants with bronchiolitis in Cork University Hospital.
audits.standard: Evidence-based guidelines recommending against routine radiological and laboratory investigations in bronchiolitis

cycle1.result: Infants under 12 months with bronchiolitis were receiving unnecessary investigations; mean average weekly CXR rate 25%.

audits.intervention: Locally agreed flowchart with regular performance feedback using run charts and in-person sessions.

cycle2.result: Mean average weekly CXR rate fell to 11% (57% reduction, p = 0.009974).

audits.other_findings: Outcome measure was weekly length of stay; balancing measure was representation rate.
audits.citation: Jansen L, Meyer GP, Curtin G, Lynch B, O'Brien R. Quality improvement project to decrease unnecessary investigations in infants with bronchiolitis in Cork University Hospital. BMJ Open Qual. 2021;10(4):e001428. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2021-001428. PMID: 34782359.

audits.title: Optimizing the Management of Pediatric Bronchiolitis: A Multi-cycle Clinical Audit at a Regional Hospital in Oman.
audits.standard: 2014 American Academy of Pediatrics Clinical Practice Guideline for bronchiolitis

cycle1.result: Chest X-ray 82% (18/22); salbutamol 91% (20/22); ipratropium 59% (13/22); corticosteroids 31% (7/22); antibiotics 45% (10/22); IV fluids 50% (11/22); nasopharyngeal suction 18% (4/22).

audits.intervention: Targeted educational and feedback interventions after each cycle.

cycle2.result: Chest X-ray 40.9% (27/66); salbutamol 22.7% (15/66); ipratropium 9% (6/66); corticosteroids 6.06% (4/66); antibiotics 15.1% (10/66); IV fluids 92.4% (61/66); suction 98.4% (65/66).

audits.other_findings: Four cycles with 210 admissions in total; all changes p < 0.001.
audits.citation: Al Maamari L, Al Shafouri N, Khaild M, Elsiddig E, Alghassani A. Optimizing the Management of Pediatric Bronchiolitis: A Multi-cycle Clinical Audit at a Regional Hospital in Oman. Cureus. 2026;18(3):e104761. doi:10.7759/cureus.104761. PMID: 41943787.

audits.title: Group-facilitated audit and feedback to improve bronchiolitis care in the emergency department.
audits.standard: Evidence-based supportive care for bronchiolitis, avoiding low-value interventions (viral testing, salbutamol, chest radiography)

cycle1.result: Low-value care 42.6% in non-admitted and 78.9% in admitted patients.

audits.intervention: Individual physician audit and feedback reports with peer comparison plus a group-facilitated feedback session.
audits.other_findings: 78% of physicians consented; ICU admissions and ED revisits unchanged.
audits.citation: Dowling SK, Gjata I, Solbak NM, Weaver CGW, Smart K, Buna R, et al.. Group-facilitated audit and feedback to improve bronchiolitis care in the emergency department. CJEM. 2020;22(5):678-686. doi:10.1017/cem.2020.374. PMID: 32484150.

audits.title: Knowledge translation in Western Australia tertiary paediatric emergency department: An audit cycle of effectiveness of guideline dissemination on bronchiolitis management.
audits.standard: Local bronchiolitis guideline based on the 2017 Australasian bronchiolitis guideline
audits.setting: Paediatric emergency department, Princess Margaret Hospital for Children, tertiary

cycle1.result: Chest X-ray 24 (5.2%), salbutamol 23 (4.9%), antibiotics 11 (2.4%), nasopharyngeal aspirate 172 (37%); admission 303 (65.2%).

audits.intervention: Dissemination of the updated local bronchiolitis guideline.

cycle2.result: Chest X-ray 17 (5.0%), salbutamol 10 (2.9%), antibiotics 5 (1.5%), nasopharyngeal aspirate 124 (36.2%); admission 192 (56.0%, P = 0.008).

audits.other_findings: No significant reduction in unnecessary interventions; glucocorticoid use 0.4% vs 1.5% and PICU admissions unchanged.
audits.citation: Yeo YL, O'Brien S, Bear N, Borland ML. Knowledge translation in Western Australia tertiary paediatric emergency department: An audit cycle of effectiveness of guideline dissemination on bronchiolitis management. J Paediatr Child Health. 2020;56(9):1358-1364. doi:10.1111/jpc.14930. PMID: 32663366.
